USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Nebulized medicine reaching the eyes

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 71-year-old patient with known narrow anterior chamber angles uses nebulized ipratropium through a poorly fitting mask. He develops eye pain, blurred vision and halos. Which drug-related complication requires urgent assessment?

  1. Central retinal artery occlusion
  2. Dry eye alone
  3. Acute angle-closure glaucoma
  4. Retinal detachment
  5. Cataract progression
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Acute angle-closure glaucoma

Ocular antimuscarinic exposure can precipitate angle closure in susceptible patients.

Understanding the options

Acute angle-closure glaucoma
Ocular antimuscarinic exposure can precipitate angle closure in susceptible patients.
Retinal detachment
Flashes, floaters and a curtain-like field defect are more typical; the painful halos after antimuscarinic exposure favor angle closure.
Cataract progression
Cataracts generally cause gradual painless visual change rather than acute painful halos.
Central retinal artery occlusion
This typically causes sudden painless vision loss, unlike the painful exposure-associated syndrome.
Dry eye alone
Mild surface irritation does not adequately explain the acute painful visual disturbance in a predisposed eye.
